name: United States of America

areaKm2.note: LoN Year-Book 1938/39 Table 2: United States 7,839 thousand km2 incl. 137k inland water, Alaska ~1,519k (printed '519' in the OCR, the leading 1 is lost), plus Hawaii ~16.6k = ~9.37M. The world_1938 polygon (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/master/geojson/world_1938.geojson) computes to ~9.25M (low).

population.note: COW NMC v7 tpop 1941 = 133,402k (1940 = 132,122k, the census year). States plus Alaska and Hawaii; the Philippines, Puerto Rico and other dependencies are not counted.

urbanization.note: HYDE via OWID: United States 1940 = 60.0% urban (high); 1940 census urban definition ~56.5% (general literature) for the mid. Low = COW upop/tpop 1941 = 38,183/133,402 = 0.286 (cities over 100,000).

activePersonnel.note: Army (incl. Army Air Forces) 1,686,403 on 31 Dec 1941 (Matloff and Snell, Strategic Planning 1941-42 ch. XVI). Navy 284,427 and Marines 54,359 at mid-1941 (National WWII Museum table, whose 1941 total 1,801,101 is the low) grew to roughly 325k and 66k by December (educated). Coast Guard (~25k) included in high.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess: the National Guard was already federalised (1940-41) and inside the active figure; recallable trained men were draftees released over age 28 in 1941, Organized Reserve officers and Navy/Marine reservists. (context page: http://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/USA/USA-WD-Strategic1/USA-WD-Strategic1-16.html)

supportPersonnel.note: active minus P roles: Army Air Forces (~350k), Navy, the Army's artillery, armored, engineer, signal and service troops, replacement-training centres and overseas garrisons (~192k overseas in Dec 1941 per the cited chapter).

mobilizationRatio.note: Peak strength 12,209,238 in 1945 (National WWII Museum table) = 0.088 of ~139M. About 16M served in total during the war (general literature, not in the fetched table) = 0.12 of the 1941 population.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Reconstruction: 37 active divisions on 31 Dec 1941 (cited chapter), ~29 of them infantry; infantry regiments of a triangular division ~9,000-10,000 at full strength, plus separate infantry regiments and the Marine Corps' two forming divisions (~30k).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: M1 Garand semi-automatic rifle standard, BAR; AT weapons weak (37 mm)

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: mostly 1940-41 draftees and Guardsmen with a year of training; Louisiana and Carolina manoeuvres 1941

count.note: 12 horse regiments of 790 horses each in Dec 1939 (Hoffmann p. 260, via the cited page): 1st and 2nd Cavalry Divisions and the 26th Cavalry (Philippine Scouts), ~1,500-1,800 men per regiment.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: horsed cavalry, obsolete for mechanised war

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: regular long-service troopers

count.note: Production 365 tanks in 1940 and 4,021 in 1941 (2,591 light, 1,430 medium; Ness, Jane's WWII Tanks p. 13 via cited page) plus a few hundred pre-1940 vehicles; more than half of M3 output went to the UK and USSR. Educated net inventory.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: M3 Stuart light and M3 Lee medium (sponson 75 mm); comparable to Pz III

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: Armored Force created July 1940, 5 armored divisions forming

count.note: Educated guess: WWI-stock 75 mm and 155 mm guns plus new 105 mm M2 howitzers (in production from 1941) and 37 mm AT guns for 37 divisions and corps units. (context page: http://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/USA/USA-WD-Strategic1/USA-WD-Strategic1-16.html)

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: 105 mm M2 and fire-direction-centre method among the era's best

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: new units, but Fort Sill gunnery school strong

count.note: Batteries. Educated guess: Coast Artillery Corps anti-aircraft regiments (3-in and new 90 mm guns, 37 mm automatic weapons) expanded in 1940-41. (context page: http://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/USA/USA-WD-Strategic1/USA-WD-Strategic1-16.html)

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: 90 mm M1 entering service, SCR-268 gun-laying radar

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: newly raised regiments

count.note: AAF Statistical Digest Table 83: fighters on hand 1,618 (end Nov 1941) and 2,170 (end Dec 1941); plus Navy and Marine fighters (F4F, F2A) ~400-700 of the Navy's ~3,400 aircraft (Underwood via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy_in_World_War_II; split educated).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: P-40, P-39, F4F Wildcat: inferior in climb and turn to the A6M Zero, rugged

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: pilot pool expanding fast; peacetime-trained cadre good

count.note: AAF Statistical Digest Table 83: heavy/medium/light bombers 157/685/350 (Nov 1941) and 288/745/799 (Dec 1941); plus Navy SBD, TBD, SB2U and PBY strike/patrol aircraft (~1,200-1,500 of ~3,400 Navy aircraft, educated split).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: B-17, SBD Dauntless good; TBD Devastator obsolete

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: expanding pilot and crew pool

count.note: NHHC ship force levels on 7 Dec 1941 (via cited page): 17 battleships, 7 fleet carriers + 1 escort carrier (Long Island), 37 cruisers. Pacific and Asiatic Fleets alone: 9 BB, 3 CV, 13 CA, 11 CL (https://historicaltextarchive.org/sections/article/194-comparative-fleet-strengths-dec-1-1941-us-japan).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: new North Carolina-class battleships and Yorktown-class carriers, CXAM radar on several ships; old battleships slow

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: long-service fleet with realistic Fleet Problems; night fighting weaker than the IJN

count.note: 171 destroyers of all types on 7 Dec 1941 (NHHC table via cited page); Pacific and Asiatic Fleets 80. High adds Coast Guard cutters and patrol vessels used as escorts.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: modern Benson/Gleaves class plus old flush-deckers; torpedo (Mk 15) defects

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: professional crews

count.note: 112 submarines on 7 Dec 1941 (NHHC via cited page); 55 in the Pacific and Asiatic Fleets.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: long-range fleet boats, but Mk 14 torpedo defective until 1943

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: professional but over-cautious peacetime doctrine

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Marshall's General Staff and Naval War College system competent; senior commanders unproven, Pearl Harbor and Philippines failures

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.5. Evidence: national conscript army just expanded; regular cadre thin; Navy and Marines stronger identity

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.5-0.75. Evidence: isolationism before 7 Dec 1941 replaced by national outrage and unity after Pearl Harbor

weapons.note: Anchor: between 7 (1905) and 8 (1943). Evidence: M1 Garand, 105 mm M2, 90 mm AA, B-17; tanks and torpedoes behind

armor.note: Anchor: between 7 and 8. Evidence: M3 Lee/Stuart riveted armour; M4 Sherman only in 1942

ships.note: Anchor: 8 (carriers, radar, submarines). Evidence: 7 fleet carriers, CXAM/SC radar, fleet submarines, fast new battleships

fortification.note: Anchor: between 7 and 8. Evidence: coast defences of harbours and the Panama Canal; Corregidor

logistics.note: Anchor: 8 (motor transport, rail). Evidence: largest truck industry in the world, dense rail and road networks, ocean shipping

communications.note: Anchor: 8 (radio at company level). Evidence: SCR-536 handie-talkie and SCR-300 coming, FM tank radios; Navy radio good

isr.note: Anchor: ISR 8 = radar. Evidence: SCR-270 radar detected the Pearl Harbor strike; signals intelligence (MAGIC)

air.note: Anchor: air 8 = 1943. Evidence: B-17, P-38 entering service, P-40, SBD; four-engine bomber force small

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (OWID CSV): United States 1940 = 12,005, 1941 = 13,553, 1942 = 14,870 (2011 int$). Range around the 1941 value.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Harrison 1998 Table 1-8: US military outlays 1% (1939), 2% (1940), 11% (1941), 31% (1942) of GNP. High = December 1941 run rate (educated).

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: manufacturing, mining and construction ~30-38% of US output around 1940. (context page: https://warwick.ac.uk/fac/soc/economics/staff/mharrison/public/ww2overview1998.pdf)

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess: the US was a large net food exporter and supplied the UK and USSR with food under Lend-Lease. (context page: https://warwick.ac.uk/fac/soc/economics/staff/mharrison/public/ww2overview1998.pdf)

annualCohort.note: LoN Year-Book 1938/39 Table 3(a): United States estimate 1935, age 20-24 both sexes = 11,382k; males ~5.7M / 5 = ~1.14M per year reaching 20.

armor.note: Harrison 1998 Table 1-6: US tanks and SPG 27.0k (1942), 38.5k (1943), 20.5k (1944).

aircraft_fighter.note: Harrison Table 1-6: combat aircraft 24.9k (1942), 54.1k (1943), 74.1k (1944); fighters ~40-50% (US fighters 99,465 of ~296k aircraft 1939-45 incl. trainers, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_production_during_World_War_II).

aircraft_strike.note: Harrison Table 1-6 combat aircraft minus fighters.

artillery.note: Harrison Table 1-6: 'guns' 188k (1942), 221k (1943), 103k (1944); note (a): roughly half were small-calibre naval and aviation weapons, so about half is taken for ground and AA artillery.

ships_major.note: 1941-45 output: 29 fleet carriers, 121 escort carriers, 10 battleships, 52 cruisers (cited page) over ~3.7 war years: ~25/yr without escort carriers, ~57/yr with them.

ships_minor.note: 396 destroyers 1941-45 (cited page) plus several hundred destroyer escorts; Harrison Table 1-6 counts 1,854-2,654 'major naval vessels' per year including small combatants.

roadKm.note: FHWA Highway Statistics Summary to 1995, Table HM-212, 1941: paved (low/intermediate and high type) rural 451,567 + urban 147,183 miles = 598,750 miles = 963,600 km. Total public roads 3,309,678 miles; high adds gravel- and stone-surfaced roads within the 'unpaved' category (educated).

railKm.note: Route mileage peaked at 254,251 miles (409,177 km) in 1916 (cited page) and had declined to roughly 233,000 miles (~376,000 km) by 1940 through abandonments (Historical Statistics figure, not fetched).

majorPorts.note: New York, Boston, Philadelphia, Baltimore, Hampton Roads, Charleston, New Orleans, Houston/Galveston, Los Angeles/San Pedro, San Francisco Bay, Puget Sound, Portland, San Diego, Pearl Harbor.

merchantTonnage.note: LoN Year-Book 1938/39 Table 113 (Lloyd's Register, June 1938): United States 11,939k gross tons incl. Great Lakes vessels (and much laid-up WWI tonnage). x1.5 to deadweight (x1.3-1.6).

supplyRangeKm.note: van Creveld, Supplying War ch. 7 (1944 Allied advance): the fully motorised US Army sustained ~400-500 km beyond railheads/ports with truck convoys; 1941 capacity lower but structurally similar.

draftAnimals.note: US horse stock 14M in 1940, down from 25M in 1920 (Gudmundsson 2004 p. 55, via cited page); the Army itself used ~52,000.

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: familiar terrain, fortified harbours, total population support; two oceans give strategic depth an invader could not cross (high 1.3), but no harsh-climate factor.

notes: Snapshot date 7 December 1941 (Pearl Harbor). United States incl. Alaska and Hawaii; the Philippine Commonwealth (Philippine Army, ~100k mobilised) is NOT included, but US forces in the Philippines (USAFFE American units, Philippine Scouts) are. Pacific Fleet share: 9 BB, 3 CV, 24 cruisers, 80 DD, 55 SS (comparative fleet strengths 1 Dec 1941). Weakest values: artillery, AA batteries and tank inventory (Lend-Lease outflow unknown), the infantry share of the Army, and trainedReserves. Production rates are 1942-44 full war economy (Harrison 1998). Ship convention: battleships, carriers, cruisers = ships_major; destroyers = ships_minor. Merchant tonnage converted to deadweight at x1.5.
